pax_corporations_tut_button_tip: Tutorial: where everything is and how to play with corporations
pax_corporations_tut_offer_text: Pax Corporations adds living corporations to the game: a thousand real companies with shares, staff, debts and development trees. Take a short tour? If you decline, you can always start it with the 🎓 button of the «Corporations» or «Development» window, and every window of the mod has a «?» — a mini tutorial of that window.
pax_corporations_tut_intro_text:
About [b]1000 real companies[/b] from 135 countries live every week: they hire and lay off people, pay wages, taxes and dividends, borrow, strike, fight rivals, take each other over, go bankrupt and are born.

They pay [b]taxes into your treasury[/b], react to your [b]laws[/b], move [b]elections[/b] and your [b]country's prestige[/b]. You rule them the way you rule the country: with orders, laws, money and stakes.
pax_corporations_tut_button_text: It all starts here — the button at the bottom opens the corporations window. The [b]red number[/b] on it is unread letters and a new summary. The mod puts the same counters on «Contacts» (countries' letters), projects and the path.
pax_corporations_tut_lists_text:
Your country's companies: market value, revenue, staff, index and the 4-week price change. Sorting and the industry filter are on the right. The [b]star[/b] adds a company to favourites — you will get its news.

On top — «Market news»: rising and falling industries and what companies pay into your treasury a year.
pax_corporations_tut_world_text: «World» — the planet's top-100 by index. «Favourites» — the companies and whole countries you marked. Click any row to open the dossier.
pax_corporations_tut_dossier_text:
Everything about a company: its world place, money, staff and their mood, its goods' market and its share, credit rating and bankruptcy chance, rivals and wars.

The [b]«Why?»[/b] button next to the staff explains why people are happy or strike. The AI button asks the game's adviser why the price moved.
pax_corporations_tut_statuses_text:
The status bars — [b]trust in the state[/b], staff satisfaction, popularity, independence, stability, monopolism, corruption, ecology. Hover a bar to see what it is made of.

Trust matters most: an unhappy company criticises the government, makes demands, backs the opposition, threatens and finally moves production abroad.
pax_corporations_tut_head_text: On the left — the company's head, role and character. [b]Click the name with the envelope ✉[/b] — the head becomes your contact and a conversation opens: negotiate, press or bargain with words like with anyone in the game.
pax_corporations_tut_shares_text: The price chart over the years, market value, rating and volatility. The price is pulled to the fair value its revenue and profit give: strikes, layoffs and crises hit it, good events lift it.
pax_corporations_tut_owners_text: Who owns the company and the state's stake. Here you can buy or sell shares at once — the green and red buttons. Foreign investors bring growth and markets but get rights: from a board seat to a blocking stake.
pax_corporations_tut_chronicle_text: Everything that happened to the company: strikes, loans, takeovers, laws, scandals, new heads. Sharp rises and falls are explained by the game's AI.
pax_corporations_tut_markets_text: Who sells how much of each goods — in the world and in a country (pie charts), corporate wars and the latest deals: takeovers, breakups, white knights.
pax_corporations_tut_arena_text: [b]Your country's prestige[/b] comes from its companies in the world top. It makes your companies' loans cheaper and the powers friendlier. Also here: which foreign companies your country depends on and who depends on yours; tariffs and sanctions; conflicts; how companies move [b]elections[/b]; corruption scandals.
pax_corporations_tut_letters_text:
Heads of companies write to you: thanks or complaints about laws, demands for compensation, threats to move, pleas for a rescue — and offers: joint projects, cheap stakes, state orders, foreign plants. [b]Accept / Decline[/b] before the deadline; silence is a refusal too.

The antimonopoly service's answers and the results of your orders come here as well.
pax_corporations_tut_summary_text: After each time skip — what mattered: events of your and favourite companies, the biggest risers and fallers, what came into the treasury.
pax_corporations_tut_found_text:
The «＋ Found a company» button: pick the goods, a name and capital from the treasury, place the headquarters on the map — the analysts count revenue, staff and wages from the market. As a ruler you found a state enterprise.

Private companies through investors are founded by an order (see below).
pax_corporations_tut_map_text:
Headquarters on the political map: size by market value, colour by industry. Neighbours fan out, big crowds are a circle with a number (click for the list). Zoomed far out — country circles.

Zoom in to see the companies' sites and lines to the headquarters; a red pulse is a strike, a red dashed line a corporate war. The layer and its mode («as is» or «country circles») are set in the layers window (Tab).
pax_corporations_tut_departments_text:
Its own bottom button: health, police, prosecutors, roads, utilities, education and the antimonopoly service. A slider sets how much of its norm a service gets; the norm is a share of the tax income. Good services raise satisfaction and productivity, cut costs and corruption.

Money above the norm works worse and is partly stolen. The antimonopoly service has a [b]mood towards the government[/b].
pax_corporations_tut_orders_text:
Companies are ruled with words — ordinary game orders naming a company:
• «Nationalise Gazprom» — a decree; «secretly take Rosneft through a front man» — a scheme.
• «Buy a controlling stake in Sberbank» — a deal; a foreign country may forbid it.
• «Rescue Aeroflot for 25% of the shares», «give it 2 billion».
• «Find investors and enthusiasts for new companies».
pax_corporations_tut_orders2_text:
• «Tax audit of Lukoil», «open a case against the head of X».
• «Start an antitrust case against Yandex».
• «30% tariffs on steel from China», «trade war with Japan», «sanctions against Samsung», «lift the tariffs on China».
• «Steal technology from Intel».

The result comes as a notification and a letter; running operations are listed in «Letters». Other countries answer serious steps — the AI picks the measure.
pax_corporations_tut_life_title: The world lives on its own
pax_corporations_tut_life_text: Without you companies compete (advertising, price wars, lawsuits, poaching), fight, take over and split, go public, go bankrupt, are born and move where it is better. Labour, tax and ecology laws change their mood. Wars between countries seize their sites and headquarters. World crises come every few years.
pax_corporations_tut_goals_text:
• [b]Money[/b]: healthy companies pay taxes, state stakes pay dividends. Don't choke business — it will leave.
• [b]Trust[/b]: watch letters and demands; a subsidy is cheaper than a lost plant.
• [b]Champions[/b]: companies in the world top give prestige — cheap loans and the powers' respect.
• [b]Services[/b]: departments pay off in happy, productive people.
• [b]Power[/b]: happy staff and loyal business help in elections; scandals and raids hurt.
• [b]World[/b]: tariffs and sanctions are weapons, but other countries answer.
pax_corporations_tut_end_text: That's all! The big tutorial is always there under 🎓, and every window of the mod has a «?» with a mini tutorial of that window. Good luck running the corporations. If you like the mod, you can always support the developer on Boosty: boosty.to/pax_yum1ko (with Pax Corpface — the orange icon next to the game's logo).

pax_corporations_tut_conditions_text: Companies depend on the country: roads, communications, energy, health, education, security and institutions where their sites are. The «Operating conditions» block of the dossier's overview shows the index and the main problem. A new power line or highway shows at once in revenue and shares; a blackout or fighting hits them.
pax_corporations_tut_caps_text: Technologies of the new time — exoskeletons, combat lasers, fusion, a Mars base — no country has them. Each needs two nodes of different industries' trees. Until you have one, orders about it are refused; a ready one can be bought from the country that developed it first.
pax_corporations_tut_development_text: The «Development» button next to «Corporations» opens the industries' trees full-screen. One tree per industry of the country; all its companies get the bonuses.
pax_corporations_tut_trees_text: Nodes cost GV — «State investments» the country builds from its companies' growth. Move along the arrows; available nodes glow blue. The bottom ★ branch is technologies: the industry's leading company develops them.
pax_corporations_tut_research_text: AI, science and space are research industries: their trees cost SD — scientific discoveries — not GV. SD build slowly, only from these industries, but each node changes the rules for the whole country: ends strikes, speeds up technologies, weakens sanctions.
pax_corporations_tut_techmap_text: All the technologies of the future: the technology in a frame, the two needed nodes of different trees running into it from below. Click a node — you land in its tree with the node lit up.
pax_corporations_tut_newspaper_text: The game's newspaper gets the loud corporate stories — share jumps, bankruptcies, company wars — and every big development step of any country: 3–4 GV nodes, SD research and new-time technologies. You learn about others' successes from rumours or official statements.
pax_corporations_tut_l_intro_text: The mod's exchange: every company of the world. On top — tabs: your country, the world top-100, favourites, markets, arena, future tech, summary and letters.
pax_corporations_tut_l_strip_text: Rising ▲ and falling ▼ industries, the top movers of 4 weeks (click — the dossier) and what companies pay into the treasury.
pax_corporations_tut_l_tools_text: Sort by index, market cap, staff or revenue and keep only one industry.
pax_corporations_tut_l_table_text: Each row is a company: place, icon with its status frame, market cap, revenue, staff, index and the 4-week change. Click a row — the dossier. Click the change — the AI assistant explains it. ☆ — favourites.
pax_corporations_tut_l_tabs2_text: «Markets» — company shares of goods markets; «Arena» — prestige, dependencies and tariffs; «Future tech» — what the country can do; «Summary» — results of a time skip; «Letters» — heads' letters with offers.
pax_corporations_tut_l_found_text: The yellow button creates a state company: choose the goods, capital and headquarters.
pax_corporations_tut_l_gear_text: The look of status frames (animated or not), frames on the map and the game interface in the mod's look.
pax_corporations_tut_l_big_text: 🎓 — the full tour of the whole mod. «?» — this mini tutorial.
pax_corporations_tut_d_head_text: The header: name, industry, country, type, share price with its change and market cap; on the right — the head (click the name to write to them).
pax_corporations_tut_d_overview_text: The company's statuses (trust, satisfaction, stability…), operating conditions, the world situation, its goods' markets, rivals and staff.
pax_corporations_tut_d_shares_text: The price chart and key figures as tiles: market cap, rating, revenue, profit, taxes, bankruptcy chance.
pax_corporations_tut_d_debt_text: How much the company owes, to whom, at what rate, and the next payments.
pax_corporations_tut_d_owners_text: The owners' donut, foreign investors and the state's buy (green) and sell (red) buttons.
pax_corporations_tut_d_assets_text: Every site: headquarters, plants, offices — with road, communications and power badges and the staff's mood. Click — show on the map.
pax_corporations_tut_d_chronicle_text: Everything that happened to the company: strikes, deals, wars, changes of conditions, discoveries.
pax_corporations_tut_d_map_text: Shows the company and its sites on the world map.
pax_corporations_tut_d_back_text: Back to the list of companies.
pax_corporations_tut_p_intro_text: Corporate taxes can pay for state services. The tiles on top: GDP, income from companies, the departments' bill, the balance, the treasury and the share of taxes.
pax_corporations_tut_p_advice_text: The advisor explains how it all works and turns red when money runs short or is stolen.
pax_corporations_tut_p_card_text: The card: percent of the norm, the yearly cost, the quality bar (it moves slowly) and the effects on companies — green helps, red hurts.
pax_corporations_tut_p_slider_text: The slider — how much of the norm the department gets: 100% is the norm, up to 200% is more, but above the norm money works worse and corruption grows.
pax_corporations_tut_p_antitrust_text: The gauge of its mood towards the government: a hostile service blocks the state's deals, a friendly one turns a blind eye.
pax_corporations_tut_p_country_text: The country's corruption and what the services do to its companies; below — comparison with other countries' services.
pax_corporations_tut_v_intro_text: The development tree of your country's industry: all its companies get the bonuses. Move from the centre along the arrows.
pax_corporations_tut_v_pick_text: Each industry has its own tree in its own style. A tree is open only if the country has companies of the industry.
pax_corporations_tut_v_wallet_text: What the nodes cost: ◆ GV — «State investments» (ordinary industries) or ⚛ SD — scientific discoveries (AI, science, space). Hover the badge or the bar next to it to see where the inflow comes from.
pax_corporations_tut_v_bar_text: The bar fills from the companies' growth; hover to see what it is made of.
pax_corporations_tut_v_advice_text: Names the industry's leading company (the link opens the dossier) or tells you there are none.
pax_corporations_tut_v_nodes_text: A blue outline — the node can be bought. Hover — description and effects; click — buy. Of the three 3-GV nodes of a branch only one can be chosen (a padlock on the others).
